messages:
evan-support: Heads-up — customer ACME running a large embedding job is getting sustained 429s from /v1/embeddings. Started ~08:12 UTC and still failing. request_id=rc-9a4f
sara-support: Got the request_id from customer, thanks. They said the job is ~5k texts sent in batches, concurrency set to 30. Paste of error: `HTTP 429 {\"error\":\"rate limit exceeded\",\"code\":\"rate_cap\"} request_id=rc-9a4f`

mike-sre: Can you paste the client payload (sanitized) + headers? Need to check concurrency + token/account rate caps. Also which model?
evan-support: Model is text-embedding-3-large, sample payload from them: ```{\n  \"model\": \"text-embedding-3-large\",\n  \"input_count\": 5000,\n  \"batch_size\": 1024,\n  \"concurrency\": 30,\n  \"expected_dim\": 1536\n}```
sara-support: They also sent an older SDK that wraps into many parallel requests, not a single bulk. They spawn 30 processes each sending batches of ~1k.
julia-ml: 30 concurrent requests × large batches sounds like a burst hitting the embedding ratecap. Embedding endpoints have both concurrent request and token/compute units limits — burst protection will 429 to protect capacity.
mike-sre: Agreed. Also check if any dimension mismatch showed in logs (client-side mismatch can force re-tries and cause higher request load). But request_id rc-9a4f shows repeated 429s in infra logs.

infra-bot: [alert] rate_cap spike detected for account acme-corp (token: acct-XX). Window: 08:11:30 - 08:13:15 UTC. 4300 requests, 28% 429 rate. Top endpoints: /v1/embeddings. Peak concurrency: 32.

evan-support: Customer is asking for a quick mitigation — they said this is blocking a batch pipeline. Any short-term suggestions?
sara-support: Suggested immediate options to customer: 1) reduce concurrency to 6-8, 2) reduce batch_size to 256-512, 3) add exponential backoff + jitter (start 100ms), 4) try spreading the job over a longer window. Asked if they'd like us to temporarily raise quota while they migrate.
mike-sre: I'll pull the ratecap dashboard and check if this account is on standard shared tier or has a reserved quota. If shared and sustained, we can offer a temporary increased concurrency allowance for tonight.
julia-ml: Also double-check that their client isn't mistakenly requesting embeddings for already-embedded items (dup requests) — dedupe helps a lot.

infra-bot: [trace] request rc-9a4f: attempts=9, last_status=429, avg_latency=220ms, queued_time=30ms. Flood pattern: many retries without jitter.

mike-sre: From logs it looks like retries are aggressive (no jitter) — that amplifies burst. I'll open a quick mitigation: enable a soft short-term throttle (per-account request smoothing) and add a one-off bump for acme-corp to let their in-flight batch drain.
evan-support: Please cc me when you do. I told customer to implement jitter + cap concurrency now.
sara-support: Customer replied they patched client to concurrency=8 + backoff with full jitter and restarted a portion of job; initial run shows success rates up from 72% -> 98% so far. They still want a postmortem and long-term advice.
julia-ml: Long-term recommendations for them: 1) use smaller batches (256-512) to smooth load; 2) use our bulk-embeddings helper or streaming where possible; 3) instrument per-request idempotency and dedupe; 4) consider Dedicated/Reserved if they need sustained high throughput.
mike-sre: I'll create an infra ticket to check if our burst window config needs tuning: ticket INF-2026. Also capture token-level traces and any kernel-schedule saturation. I'll attach flame charts.
evan-support: Thanks. Customer asked if dimension mismatch could be related — they reported the expected dimension 1536. Do we see any errors like dimension mismatch?\ulia-ml: (typo) julia-ml: We don't see any dim-mismatch errors in the logs for rc-9a4f. That usually returns 400 with a clear schema error; this is purely rate_cap 429s.
sara-support: I'll send the customer a summary of the immediate actions + recommended retry/backoff snippet: ```python
# exponential backoff (jittered)
import random, time
base=0.1
for attempt in range(6):
  try:
    # call embeddings API
    break
  except RateLimitError:
    sleep = base * (2 ** attempt) * (0.5 + random.random()/1.0)
    time.sleep(sleep)
```

infra-bot: [note] temporary per-account smoothing applied at 08:18 UTC, bump TTL: 30m.

evan-support: Customer confirms job finished after reducing concurrency and adding retries. They asked about prevention — want guidance doc and maybe a quota increase request form.
julia-ml: Sara, can you send them the embeddigns best-practices doc and link to the quota-request form. Also recommend a short pilot on Dedicated if they expect sustained >10k reqs/day.
sara-support: On it. I'll follow up with a brief incident summary and link to best-practices + quota increase next steps. Tagging this resolved for now but leaving infra ticket open for tune analysis. :white_check_mark:
